flawed_step: The claim diam = 2·rad is true only for trees whose diameter is even. Any tree with an odd diameter breaks it, because then diam = 2·rad − 1.
counterexample: Take the tree T = K2 (the path P2): n = 2, vertices a and b, one edge ab. d(a,b) = 1, so diam(T) = 1. The eccentricity of a is 1 and of b is 1, so rad(T) = 1. That gives 2·rad(T) = 2 ≠ 1 = diam(T). Another example is P4 with n = 4: diam = 3, rad = 2, and 2·2 = 4 ≠ 3.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. For trees, diam = 2·rad − 1 when the diameter is odd. The path on 2 vertices (diam 1, rad 1) meets the hypothesis 2 ≤ n ≤ 7 and fails the equation.
